subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase/stagger or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, and should heartbeat expose any public knob beyond its current automatic stable phase?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining change defines public scheduling semantics and config/protocol shape that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add focused public `every` phase/stagger semantics with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Document current supported behavior
options.body: Keep fixed `everyMs`/`anchorMs` semantics and document heartbeat automatic phase spreading plus cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron with explicit migration, observability, and compatibility requirements.

recommendation.title: Design cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add focused public `every` phase/stagger semantics with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current cron stagger contract and has the strongest history on the public scheduler/API boundary in this area.
